body:
Title: `uv python pin` and `uv lock` write through repo-shipped `.python-version` / `uv.lock` symlinks

Body:

A repository can ship `.python-version` or `uv.lock` as a symlink,
and uv writes through the link to its target, outside the project.

Verified on uv 0.13.9:

1. `.python-version` as a symlink (the stronger case): `uv python
   pin 3.13` clobbers the symlink's target with no content gate.
   A victim file elsewhere on the machine is truncated to `3.13`;
   if the symlink dangles into an existing parent directory, the
   file is created at that chosen path. Either way the symlink
   itself is preserved. Root: `write_atomic_preserve`
   (`crates/uv-fs/src/lib.rs:501-566`, documented as "preserving
   symlinks... a missing symlink target is created when its parent
   directory exists"), reached ungated from
   `crates/uv-python-discovery/src/version_files.rs:289-304`.

2. `uv.lock` as a symlink: `uv lock` and `uv sync` write through to
   the target as well, with one mitigating gate — uv parses the
   existing lock before committing, so a target holding arbitrary
   content fails the TOML parse and nothing is written; a target
   holding a valid lock is rewritten, and dangling targets are
   created at the chosen path. Reached from
   `crates/uv-lock-operations/src/lock_target.rs:405`.

Reproduction: in a scratch project, `ln -s /tmp/victim.txt
.python-version`, put known content in the victim, run
`uv python pin 3.13`; the victim now contains `3.13`. Control:
with a regular `.python-version`, the write stays in the project.

The write-through is deliberate (the doc comment on
`write_atomic_preserve` states symlink preservation as the design,
and #22399/#22402 describe preserving symlink targets and modes as
publication policy), but here the victim never chose the target —
the repository did by shipping the link, and the write lands on a
file outside the repository the pin command was never authorized to
touch. #21857/#21891 (a repo-tracked symlink redirecting a write
outside the checkout, labeled bug and fixed) looks like the same
class.

Suggested direction: for these project-state files, either write to
the literal path (replacing the symlink) rather than its target, or
refuse to follow a symlink unless the target is inside the project
directory.

A self-verifying PoC script with canary files and clean controls is
available on request. All testing was local.
title: uv python pin and uv lock write through repo-shipped .python-version / uv.lock symlinks
